design: docs/research/CORE_REALTIME_B2.md, P4 plan (2026-10-08): every pass is a direct child of the gameplay body's single copy, so a pass whose whole chain runs in place saves its copies whatever its siblings do; P4a's partial attempt (reverted) explains why the whole chain is needed
profile_before: rt4w-dwarf (4w tree): copies of OriginalStateRecord 16.2% of the main thread inclusive, freed record arrays 12.0%; WorldControl's copy levels (its pool and globals, ActorControl's candidate and Body, ActorInput's candidate) and the same shape in physics; a 92 KB globals copy for every actor that draws or queues a sound
change: ActorInput, ActorControl, WorldControl, ActorPhysics, WorldPhysics and the post-draw lifecycle get an in-place form: the caller's records (and the lifecycle's scratch) move into the pass or body with inPlaceTake and are written back by a defer on every path; per actor the helper runs on &pool[i]. The default forms copy, run the in-place form and assign on success, so their errors and order are unchanged. State-level entries are package applyInPlace (P4b's review); the gameplay body, which commits only at its end and has no catch, switches control, physics and lifecycle to them
